_comment: Federal depreciation rules by year. Every value carries source_url, source_citation and last_verified. Each figure was read from the cited IRS PDF (downloaded and parsed 2026-10-05); see docs/tax-research/depreciation-macrs-179-bonus-280f-2021-2026.md and docs/depreciation-calculator-PROGRESS.md. Update yearly: see README 'Depreciation calculator - yearly rule update'.

assumptions.value: Calendar-year taxpayer with a full 12-month tax year. The percentage tables cannot be used for a short tax year.
assumptions.source_citation: IRS Pub. 946 (2025), ch. 4, 'Rules Covering the Use of the Tables', rule 2

mid_quarter_test.value: Mid-quarter convention applies if more than 40% of the depreciable basis of MACRS property placed in service in the year (excluding residential rental and nonresidential real property) is placed in service in the last 3 months. Basis reflects section 179 and personal use, but not the special depreciation allowance.
mid_quarter_test.source_citation: IRS Pub. 946 (2025), ch. 4, 'Which Convention Applies?', mid-quarter convention and Caution

2021.source_citation: 2021 Instructions for Form 4562, What's New and Part I

2022.source_citation: 2022 Instructions for Form 4562, What's New and Part I

2023.source_citation: 2023 Instructions for Form 4562, What's New and Part I

2024.source_citation: 2024 Instructions for Form 4562, What's New and Part I

2025.source_citation: 2025 Instructions for Form 4562, What's New (P.L. 119-21 sec. 70306; supersedes Rev. Proc. 2024-40 amounts of $1,250,000 / $3,130,000)

section_179_income_limit.value: The section 179 deduction cannot exceed taxable income from the active conduct of any trade or business (computed without the section 179 deduction); the disallowed amount carries forward. Basis is reduced by the amount elected even when part of it carries forward.
section_179_income_limit.source_citation: 2025 Instructions for Form 4562, Lines 11-13; IRC 179(b)(3); Treas. Reg. 1.179-1(f)(2)

rules.label: Qualified property acquired after Sept. 27, 2017 and before Jan. 20, 2025
rules.source_citation: Instructions for Form 4562: 2021 ('100% ... placed in service before January 1, 2023'), 2022 (80% for 2023), 2023/2024 (60% for 2024), 2025 (40% for property acquired before Jan. 20, 2025); IRC 168(k)(6) as in effect before P.L. 119-21 (20% for 2026)

rules.label: Qualified property acquired after Jan. 19, 2025

reduced_rate_election.value: Election to take 40% instead of 100% for property placed in service during the first taxable year ending after Jan. 19, 2025 (tax year 2025 for a calendar-year taxpayer).

rules.binding_contract_rule: Property is not treated as acquired after Jan. 19, 2025 if a written binding contract for its acquisition was entered into before that date.
rules.source_citation: Notice 2026-11, sec. 2 (P.L. 119-21 sec. 70301); 2025 Instructions for Form 4562, What's New

eligibility.value: Qualified property is MACRS property with a recovery period of 20 years or less (including qualified improvement property). Buildings (27.5- and 39-year property) are not qualified property. Listed property must be used more than 50% for business. The election out applies to all property in a class placed in service in the year.
eligibility.source_citation: Instructions for Form 4562, Line 14 (qualified property); IRC 168(k)(2), 168(k)(7)

qualified_production_property.value: Elective 100% allowance for the portion of nonresidential real property used as an integral part of a qualified production activity. Office, administrative, lodging, parking, sales and similar space is excluded. Recapture under section 1245 if the use changes within 10 years.
qualified_production_property.source_citation: Notice 2026-16 (IRC 168(n), P.L. 119-21 sec. 70307); 2025 Instructions for Form 4562, What's New

luxury_auto_caps._comment: IRC 280F(a) limits for passenger automobiles (6,000 lb GVWR or less) by placed-in-service year: [1st year, 2nd year, 3rd year, each succeeding year]. with_bonus = Table 1 (168(k) applies), without_bonus = Table 2.

2025.source_citation: Rev. Proc. 2025-16, Tables 1 and 2 (unchanged by P.L. 119-21 per Rev. Proc. 2026-15)

luxury_auto_100pct_safe_harbor.value: When a passenger automobile takes 100% bonus and the first-year 280F limit applies, years 2-6 apply the MACRS table percentage for that year to the remaining adjusted depreciable basis (basis minus the first-year limit), each capped by that year's 280F limit; unrecovered basis is deducted after the recovery period at the succeeding-year limit.
luxury_auto_100pct_safe_harbor.verify_note: Rev. Proc. 2019-13 was not re-read in this research pass; mechanics are from its published example. Flagged for review.

listed_property.value: Listed property (passenger automobiles and other property used for transportation) used 50% or less for qualified business use must use ADS straight line and cannot take section 179 or the special depreciation allowance.
listed_property.source_citation: IRS Pub. 946 (2025), ch. 5 and Table 4-1 ('ADS using SL: listed property used 50% or less for business')

clean_vehicle_credit_basis.value: Basis of a vehicle is reduced by any clean vehicle credit claimed for it before depreciation is figured.
clean_vehicle_credit_basis.verify_note: Statute cited from standing knowledge; not re-read in this research pass.

recapture_note.value: On a sale, depreciation taken on personal property (including section 179 and bonus) is recaptured as ordinary income under section 1245 up to the gain. On buildings, gain attributable to straight-line depreciation is 'unrecaptured section 1250 gain', taxed at up to 25%. A state that disallowed bonus has a different basis, so the state gain differs too.
recapture_note.verify_note: Informational note; Pub. 544 not re-read in this pass.

form_4562_lines._comment: Form 4562 line references. The 2025 form added line 19h (50-year property), moving residential rental to 19i and nonresidential real to 19j. The 2026 form is not yet published; the 2025 layout is assumed.

layouts.source_citation: Form 4562 (2025), Parts I-V (2026 form assumed identical until published)
